course_name_original: Pedagogie I (Fundamentele educatiei. Teoria metodologia curriculumului)
course_name_en: Pedagogy I (The Fundamentals of Pedagogy. Curriculum Theory and Methodology)
prerequisites: Completion of the discipline Educational Psychology
Identifies learning objectives in accordance with curricular documents, which support the development of each child/student/young person's potential.

learning_outcomes.text: Presents specific contents of the field and correlates the main theories and methodological orientations of learning from the perspective of pedagogical design.
Describes concepts, theories, principles, procedures, and methods specific to the educational field.
Develops and experiments adaptable models/structures in relation to the evolution of pedagogical paradigms.
Identifies values, principles, paradigms, fundamental concepts of curriculum design, development, implementation, and evaluation, instruction, and structuring of the didactic process.
Correlates the implications of current main legislative benchmarks and educational policies.

Explains (Establishes & maintains) behavioral/organizational norms and rules for educational activities, facilitating the accountability of children/students/young people, mutual respect, and trust relationships.
Analyzes and correlates psycho-pedagogical knowledge in training activities and continuous improvement of professional practices.
Integrates ethical norms, academic integrity, and professional conduct.
Applies the curriculum by following the specific stages and methodologies for carrying out activities in the educational process.
Organizes educational activities and strategies used for training children/students/young people/groups by referring to standards and objectives mentioned in curricular documents.
Identifies learning objectives in accordance with curricular documents, which support the development of each child/student/young person's potential.
Adapts relevant content for the development of specific competencies, pursued according to the curriculum.
Uses/Identifies the programmatic documents of the educational unit as support for making managerial decisions in different educational contexts.
Prepares and utilizes alternative spaces, outside the classroom or educational unit, for significant learning experiences.
Applies legal regulations concerning the education system and current educational policies.
Initiates collaborations in the sustainable development of the school, by initiating and carrying out specific actions at the institutional level.
Autonomously uses norms, standards, curricular objectives, and specific methodologies in designing/implementing educational programs/projects/interventions/actions.
Critically approaches the responsibilities of the teaching profession, highlighting the complexity of the educational process.
Communicates effectively by providing constructive feedback and supports active involvement of students in their own learning process.
Maintains a positive atmosphere in the classroom and school, cultivating belonging to the educational community.
Specifically supports the promotion of correctness, objectivity, justice, adopts stimulating and non-discriminatory educational practices.
Expresses confidence in the developmental potential of each child/student/young person and supports their aspirations through differentiated and individualized didactic approaches.
Supports the socio-emotional and moral development of students.
Adapts conduct based on reflection on stereotypes and preconceptions related to race, ethnicity, gender, socio-economic and cultural status, age, ability, religion, or nationality.
Manifests positive, active, creative, reflexive attitudes, and a critical spirit towards the teaching profession and their own continuous training.
Promotes the image of the institution and their own profession by getting involved in various educational projects/programs.
Manages the digital educational environment safely, responsibly, and ethically, in accordance with the characteristics and needs of children/students/young people to optimize learning.

syllabus_topics: Pedagogy and the system of educational sciences. Education as a subject of study of pedagogy. Functions of education. Factors of education.
Forms of education: formal, non-formal, informal.
Components of education: intellectual education, moral-civic education, technological education, aesthetic education, professional education, physical education.
Contemporary world issues and new educations.
Curriculum theory issues.
Types of curriculum.
Educational finalities: conceptualization, history.
Ideal, purpose, objectives. Competency-based education.
Curricular contents.
Curricular products: framework curriculum plan, school curriculum, alternative textbooks, curricular guides, support materials.
Thematic presentation, bibliography, objectives, and evaluation criteria.
Forms of education: formal, non-formal, informal. Comparative analysis exercises.
Classic dimensions of education. Analysis of dimensions through group activities.
New educations. Their interdependence with forms of education. Group activities.
The concept of "curriculum" and the new curricular vision: what curriculum is and isn't; curriculum vs. instruction. Exercises and group activities.
Educational finalities: types of finalities. Operationalization of educational objectives. Exercises for operationalizing educational objectives.
Curricular design documents. Framework curriculum plan: structure analysis. Timetable. School curriculum: analysis, structure.
Optional curriculum. Development of an optional discipline curriculum at the initiative of the teacher. Presentation, model analysis. Exercises for developing an optional discipline curriculum.
Textbooks, didactic auxiliaries. Analysis of textbooks, didactic auxiliaries, digital textbook.
Curricular design. Development of specific documents for annual design/calendar planning.
Synthesis seminar: analyses, debates, evaluation of seminar activity.
teaching_methods: Digital applications for systematization and recapitalization of knowledge
assessment_rules: The final evaluation result requires a minimum final grade of 5.
